requirements.title: GENERIC statements specify generic identifiers for specific procedures
requirements.definition: A GENERIC statement specifies a generic identifier for one or more specific procedures in the same way as a generic interface block that does not contain interface bodies.

pending.generic-stmt-specifies-generic-identifie: Compile/run a module with GENERIC :: gen => s_int, s_logical; gen(-5) reaches s_int and returns exact 37, while gen(.true.) reaches s_logical and returns .false. Companion direct calls to s_int(-5) and s_logical(.true.) expect the same exact values, making wrong generic resolution observable.
pending.generic-stmt-equivalent-to-procedure-onl: Compile/run paired modules, one using GENERIC :: gen => s and one using INTERFACE gen; MODULE PROCEDURE s; END INTERFACE, with s(i)=42+i. Calls through both generic identifiers with -5 change sentinels to exact 37; companion direct specific calls also produce 37, exposing any wrong binding.

requirements.title: GENERIC statements have optional access and a specific procedure list
requirements.definition: A generic-stmt is GENERIC, an optional access-spec, double colon, a generic-spec, =>, and a specific-procedure-list.

pending.generic-stmt-basic-form: Valid control: module m contains GENERIC :: gen => s and a contained subroutine s. Negative source-control removes => only; expect syntax rejection.
pending.generic-stmt-access-spec: Valid control: module m contains GENERIC, PUBLIC :: gen => s and a contained subroutine s. Negative source-control writes GENERIC PUBLIC :: gen => s; expect syntax rejection.
pending.generic-stmt-specific-procedure-list: Valid control: GENERIC :: gen => s, t lists two contained procedures. Negative source-control leaves GENERIC :: gen => with no procedure name; expect syntax rejection.

requirements.title: GENERIC statements cannot repeat an accessible procedure for the same generic identifier
requirements.definition: A specific-procedure in a GENERIC statement shall not specify a procedure that was specified previously in any accessible interface with the same generic identifier.

pending.generic-stmt-no-duplicate-accessible-spe: Rejected program: MODULE m contains INTERFACE gen; MODULE PROCEDURE s; END INTERFACE and later GENERIC :: gen => s, with contained distinguishable functions s(i)=42+i and t(l)=.not. l. Positive control keeps the same generic identifier gen and changes only the duplicated specific in the GENERIC statement from s to distinct specific t; calls gen(-5) and gen(.true.) expect exact 37 and .false., proving the legal extension of the same generic.

requirements.title: GENERIC statement access specifications set generic accessibility
requirements.definition: If access-spec appears in a GENERIC statement, it specifies the accessibility of the generic-spec.

pending.generic-stmt-public-accessibility: Compile/run provider module with PRIVATE default and GENERIC, PUBLIC :: gen => s where s(i)=42+i; client USEs gen and call gen(-5) changes sentinel to exact 37. Companion direct provider-internal call s(-5) also returns 37, while a hidden local gen returning 5 would expose wrong accessibility resolution.
pending.generic-stmt-private-accessibility: Negative source-control: change only PUBLIC to PRIVATE in that provider and keep client USE of gen; expect accessibility rejection without asserting diagnostic wording. Positive companion keeps PUBLIC and uses s(i)=42+i with gen(-5) returning exact 37 so a wrong private/local resolution is observable.
